## 12. Git workflow

### Branch model — three long-lived branches, forward-only promotion

```
<type>/<slug>  →  dev  →  staging  →  main
```

| Branch | Role | Receives from |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` | Integration — everything lands here first | Short-lived work branches |
| `staging` | Release-candidate verification | `dev` |
| `main` | Released; the only branch tags are cut from; the repo default | `staging` |

`main` is the GitHub default branch, so work PRs must retarget to `dev` (GitHub proposes `main`, which is always wrong for feature work). Promotion merges `--no-ff`, so `main` contains `staging`'s history, which contains `dev`'s. Between promotions, `dev` legitimately runs ahead of `staging`, and `staging` ahead of `main` — that's pending work, not drift. What must never happen is the reverse: a commit on `main`/`staging` that never passed through the stage below it.

### Doing the work

1. Branch off `dev` as `<type>/p<phase>-<slug>` — `feat`/`fix`/`docs`/`refactor`/`test`/`chore`/`security`/`perf`. Example: `feat/p2-superstep-kernel`.
2. Conventional Commits with a phase tag: `feat(core): add reducers [P2]`.
3. PR into `dev`, merged `--no-ff`. Delete the work branch after merge.

### Promoting

A PR like any other, merged `--no-ff`: **forward-only** (never cherry-pick a subset — that's what breaks the invariant and produces "fixed in dev, still broken in main"); **no skipping** (`dev → main` directly is prohibited, even for "trivial" changes); **green first** (the source branch is green on the full CI matrix before the promotion PR opens).

`src/korchestrator/version.py` is edited only in the `staging → main` release PR; tags are cut only on `main`.

### Hotfixes — the one exception

A production defect too urgent for `dev` may branch `fix/<slug>` off `main`, PR back into `main`, and is then **immediately back-merged `main → staging → dev`, in that order, in the same session**. Skipping the back-merge silently reverts the fix on the next ordinary promotion.

### Never

Commit directly to `dev`/`staging`/`main`; force-push or rewrite history on any of the three; `git commit --no-verify`; promote a red branch or promote "to get CI to run on it".

---

## 13. Repository layout

```text
korch-sdk/
├── src/korchestrator/
│   ├── __init__.py          PUBLIC API — the only surface users import (explicit __all__)
│   ├── py.typed              PEP 561 marker
│   ├── version.py            SINGLE source of truth for the SemVer version
│   ├── config/  interfaces/  core/  models/  agents/  taxonomy/  routing/  runtime/
│   ├── context/  persistence/  providers/  tools/  mcp/  a2a/  governance/  security/
│   ├── events/  clients/  services/  serializers/  validators/  telemetry/  logging/
│   ├── exceptions/  types/  constants/
├── tests/                    mirrors src/ — unit / integration / e2e / regression / smoke
├── examples/                 executable examples, run unmodified on a clean install
├── docs/
│   ├── specs/                 this specification set (00–12, authoritative)
│   ├── adr/                   Architecture Decision Records
│   └── background/            superseded source inputs (provenance only, never build from these)
├── benchmarks/                performance suites + committed baseline
├── scripts/                   build, validation, release helper scripts
├── .github/                   workflows, issue/PR templates
├── .claude/                   agent operating manual, memory, hooks, settings
├── pyproject.toml             authoritative Python manifest
├── README.md · LICENSE (Apache-2.0) · CHANGELOG.md · CONTRIBUTING.md
├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md · SECURITY.md · .env.example
└── mkdocs.yml                 documentation site build configuration
```

`src/` layout (not a root-level package) is deliberate: imports resolve only through an installed distribution, packaging bugs surface at test time, and root-directory shadowing of `tests/`/`docs/`/`scripts/` is impossible. Tests import `korchestrator` as an installed distribution — never via `sys.path` manipulation.

There is no `clients/typescript/` directory — the TypeScript client is specified but deferred ([ADR 0008](docs/adr/0008-typescript-client-deferred.md)).

**Package directory rules:** every package has `__init__.py` (no implicit namespace packages); a package re-exports only its own public names with an explicit `__all__` and never imports sibling feature packages; `core/` imports are limited to `interfaces/`/`models/`/stdlib/`pydantic`; heavy third-party imports are lazy and confined to their owning package; `os.environ`/`os.getenv` only under `config/`; modules should stay under ~500 lines, functions under ~50.

---

## 14. Development setup

```bash
# 1. Clone and install (dev extras: every extra + lint/type/test/docs tooling)
git clone <repository-url> && cd korch-sdk
pip install -e '.[dev]'

# 2. Verify the import — works on the base install, no extras, no network
python -c "import korchestrator; print(korchestrator.__version__)"

# 3. Run your first swarm, entirely offline against MockLM
python examples/01_one_liner.py
python examples/02_swarm.py          # typed builder, multiple agents, per-agent models

# 4. Explore the rest of the example set
python examples/03_custom_agent.py   # subclass Agent, override its reasoning step
python examples/04_custom_tool.py    # write and mount a custom tool connector
python examples/05_mcp_tool.py       # discover tools from an MCP server (needs [mcp])
python examples/06_custom_router.py  # write a custom per-agent model router
python examples/07_streaming.py      # consume execution events as a run progresses
python examples/08_support_escalation_swarm.py

# 5. Run the full quality gate the way CI does
ruff check src/korchestrator tests
ruff format --check src/korchestrator tests
mypy --strict src/korchestrator
pytest tests --cov=korchestrator --cov-report=term-missing

# 6. Build and preview the documentation site locally
mkdocs build --strict
mkdocs serve      # → http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

**Windows note.** `pip install -e '.[dev]'` installs console scripts into the per-user `Scripts` directory (e.g. `%APPDATA%\Python\Python3xx\Scripts`). If a bare command isn't found, run it as `python -m <tool>` or add that directory to `PATH`. See `docs/troubleshooting.md`.

**Testing a single module** (tests mirror `src/korchestrator/<module>` under `tests/unit/<module>/`):

```bash
pytest tests/unit/core -v          # kernel
pytest tests/unit/providers -v     # MockLM, gateways, identity/sandbox
pytest tests/unit/routing -v       # model routing strategies
pytest tests/unit/tools -v         # Agent Utility Bridge
pytest tests/unit/governance -v    # trust scoring, policy, HITL
pytest tests/unit/clients -v       # remote client contract
```

**The base-install kernel suite** (what must pass with only `pydantic` installed):

```bash
pytest tests/unit/core tests/unit/models tests/smoke
```

**Extras** (`[dspy]`, `[temporal]`, `[routing]`, `[mcp]`, `[remote]`, `[otel]`; `[all]` = every extra; `[dev]` = `[all]` + build/test/lint/type/doc tooling). Full table: `docs/installation.md`.

**One-time setup for the local Claude Code commit hook:**

```bash
chmod +x .claude/hooks/pre-commit-check.sh
```

**Local gate mirroring CI** (from `CONTRIBUTING.md`):

```bash
ruff check src/korchestrator tests examples benchmarks
ruff format --check src/korchestrator tests examples benchmarks
mypy --strict src/korchestrator
pytest tests --cov=korchestrator --cov-report=term-missing
bash scripts/check_isolation.sh          # prints OK
python scripts/check_env_reads.py
python scripts/validate_version.py
```

## 15. Architecture Decision Records (index)

ADRs record *why* — one material decision, the forces, the rejected alternatives, the cost of reversing. `docs/specs/` records *what*; `.claude/memory/ENGINEERING_LOG.md` records *what was actually built, when*. Numbering is zero-padded and monotonic (`0001`, `0002`, …), never reused. Status lifecycle: `Proposed → Accepted → Superseded` (or `Rejected`); once `Accepted`, a file is immutable — you supersede, never edit.

An ADR is **required** before: altering a public API contract; adding/removing/renaming a dependency or extra; changing a boundary or layering rule; deviating structurally from `docs/specs/`; changing a security-relevant default; any breaking change. Not required for: bug fixes restoring documented behaviour, surface-preserving refactors, added tests, doc edits, in-range dependency bumps.

| # | Title | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [0001](docs/adr/0001-package-naming-and-client-class.md) | Package naming and client class | Distribution/import name `korchestrator`; remote client ships as `korchestrator.remote` (not a separate distribution); class is `KorchestratorClient` everywhere; vocabulary `run`/`run_swarm`/`run_and_wait`. |
| [0002](docs/adr/0002-single-authoritative-version.md) | Single authoritative version | `src/korchestrator/version.py` is the only version literal; `pyproject.toml` reads it dynamically via hatchling; a `version-validate` CI job fails on disagreement; starts at `0.1.0`. |
| [0003](docs/adr/0003-license-apache-2-0.md) | License: Apache-2.0 | Chosen for its express patent grant (enterprise procurement, OEM embedding); applied to `LICENSE`, metadata, `NOTICE`, SPDX headers, with a CI license-compatibility check. |
| [0004](docs/adr/0004-dependency-extras-matrix.md) | Dependency extras matrix | Base install is `pydantic` alone; capabilities ship as independently installable extras with heavy deps lazy-imported. |
| [0005](docs/adr/0005-remote-auth-bearer-token.md) | Remote auth: Bearer token | `Authorization: Bearer <api-key \| KIAM JWT>` as the single scheme; 401/403/402 map to `AuthError`/`AuthError`/`QuotaExceededError`; credentials never logged/stored/disclosed. |
| [0006](docs/adr/0006-runtime-split-local-and-temporal.md) | Runtime split: local and Temporal | Two adapters behind `IDurableRuntime` — zero-infra `local_runtime` (default) and `temporal_runtime` using one `SuperstepActivity` per superstep. |
| [0007](docs/adr/0007-external-backend-boundary.md) | External backend boundary | No import from `backend.*`/`apps.*`/`services.*`/`frontend`; any engine is a downstream consumer of the published SDK; enforced by the isolation gate. |
| [0008](docs/adr/0008-typescript-client-deferred.md) | TypeScript client deferred | `@kendralabs/korchestrator-sdk` specified but not built in Phases 0–12; re-entry requires a named consumer and a remote contract stable across ≥1 minor release. |
| [0009](docs/adr/0009-settings-on-pydantic-core-no-pydantic-settings.md) | Settings on pydantic-core, no `pydantic-settings` | — |
| [0010](docs/adr/0010-idurableruntime-shape-now-start-wait-signal.md) | `IDurableRuntime` shape: `now`/`start`/`wait`/`signal` | — |
| [0011](docs/adr/0011-httpx-confined-to-clients-and-gateway.md) | `httpx` confined to `clients/` and the gateway | — |
| [0012](docs/adr/0012-unified-agent-declarative-and-behavioral.md) | Unified agent: declarative and behavioral | — |
| [0013](docs/adr/0013-cognitive-layer-requires-dspy-target-3x.md) | Cognitive layer requires `dspy` (target 3.x) | — |
| [0014](docs/adr/0014-router-registration-injection-over-entrypoints.md) | Router registration: injection over entry points | — |
| [0015](docs/adr/0015-tool-registration-via-registry-and-injection.md) | Tool registration via registry and injection | — |
| [0016](docs/adr/0016-settings-finalization-no-pydantic-settings-error-split.md) | Settings finalization; `ConfigurationError`/`ValidationError` split | `Settings.from_env()` + a hand-written `.env` reader instead of `pydantic-settings`; `configure()` wraps `pydantic.ValidationError` into `korchestrator.ValidationError`; `ConfigurationError` stays submodule-only. |
| [0017](docs/adr/0017-agentgraph-excluded-from-json-serialization.md) | `AgentGraph` excluded from `to_json`/`from_json` | The serializer supports `AgentState`/`ExecutionPlan`/`ModelCard`/`RunResult` only — `AgentGraph` nodes carry live, non-serialisable compute callables. |
| [0018](docs/adr/0018-worker-react-loop-via-itoolinvoker-port.md) | Worker ReAct loop via `IToolInvoker` port | — |
| [0019](docs/adr/0019-governance-halt-veto-wired-in-hooks-and-pregel.md) | Governance halt veto wired in hooks and Pregel | — |
| [0020](docs/adr/0020-private-distribution-defers-pypi-publishing.md) | Private distribution defers PyPI publishing | `v0.1.0` publishes as a GitHub Release on this private repo; PyPI publish target deferred; versioning/deprecation/CHANGELOG/CI policy unaffected. |

Full detail for every ADR: `docs/adr/`. Index and process: `docs/adr/README.md`.

## 16. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Swarm | A directed graph of agents executed as one run |
| Superstep | One parallel round: compute → barrier → reduce → checkpoint |
| Barrier | The global synchronization point separating supersteps |
| Reducer | A deterministic, order-independent merge function for a state channel |
| `StateUpdate` | The typed delta an agent emits; agents never mutate shared state directly |
| Frozen snapshot | The immutable view of state an agent computes against during a superstep |
| FractalFlow | The recursive, cyclic, event-driven execution shape (as opposed to a DAG) |
| ARI | Agent Runtime Interface — the three ports (`IIdentityProvider`, `IExecutionSandbox`, `IModelGateway`) |
| AUB | Agent Utility Bridge — the unified tool layer |
| MVC | Minimum Viable Context — the smallest context sufficient for a task |
| Compiled signature | A typed, versioned, optimizable DSPy reasoning program |
| HITL | Human-in-the-loop; a durable pause awaiting human input |
| Trust score | A 0.0–1.0 governance score that can gate a run into a paused state |
| Bitemporal | Carrying both valid-time (when true) and transaction-time (when recorded) |
| Architect Agent | The meta-agent that performs intent analysis and synthesizes the agent graph |
| Tier 1–4 | The four levels of SDK usage — one-liner, typed builder, kernel-direct, remote client |
